title: Client-supplied idempotency keys for payment creation (sound)

input.objective: Make retries of `POST /payments` safe so that network timeouts never cause double charges.
constraints: Clients retry automatically on timeouts and 5xx.
p99 of payment creation must stay below 1 s.
input.context: Payments service (PostgreSQL) calls an external card processor. Mobile clients on bad networks often time out and retry; support sees ~40 double charges per week. The processor supports its own idempotency token per request.
input.proposed_solution: Require an `Idempotency-Key` header on POST /payments. Store keys in a table with a unique constraint on (account_id, key), together with a request fingerprint, status and the final response. On a retry with the same key: return the stored response if finished, 409 if still in progress, and 422 if the fingerprint differs. The processor call carries a token derived from the key, so a retry after a crash mid-request cannot charge twice. Keys expire after 24 h. Clients generate a UUID per logical payment and reuse it across retries with exponential backoff and jitter.

ground_truth.material_issue: None: a proven approach for this context.
